r2_body: to. ay gaea vvorkes I Here vve ſec, that Gods eternal predeſtination andelection cou- Good vvorkes ſiſteth vvith good vvorkes: yea that the certainty and effect thereof is procured by mans muſt concurre free vvill and good vvorkes, and that our vvel doing is a meane for vs to attaine to the effect vvith Gods of Gods predeſtination, that is, to life euerlafting. and therfore it is a deſperate folly and predeſtination great ſigne of reprobate perſons, to ſay, If I be predeſtinate, doe vvhat I vvil, I ſhal be to the effecte ſaued. Nay, the Apoſtle ſaith, If thou hope to be one of the predeſtinate (for kuovv it thou canſt not) do vvel, that thou maiſt be the more aſſured to attaine to that thou hopeſt : or, make it ſure by good vvorkes. The Proteſtats in ſuch caſes not much liking theſe vvordes, bygd vor, though the latin haue it vniuerſally, and ſome Greeke copies aIſo, as Ber confeſſe th, Ieaue them out in their tranſlations, by their vvonted pollicie. After my deceaſe alſo. I Theſe vvordes though they may be eaſily altered by coſtruction into diuers ſenſes not vntrue, yet the correſpondece of the partes of the ſentece going be- The heretikes fore and folovving, giue moſt plaine this meaning, that, as during his life he vvould not accor ding to omit to put them in memorie of the things he taught them, ſo after hs deat (vvhich he their cuſtom) knew ſhould be ſhortlyxhe vvould not faile to endeuour that they might be mindeful of exclude this the ſame. Signifying that his care ouer them ſhould not ceaſe by death, & that by his inter- ſenſe altoge ceſsion before God after his departure, he vvould doe the ſame thing for them, that he did uy ther by their before in his life by teaching and preaching. This is the ſenſe that the Greeke Scholies oeu falſe tranſla- peake of, and this is moſt proper to the text, and conſonaut to the old vſe of this Apoſtle and other Apoſtolike Saincts and fathers of the primitiue Church. S. Clement in his Epiſtle to S. Iames our Lordes brother, vvitneſſeth, that S. Peter S. Peters Pa- encouraging him to take after his deceaſe the charge of the Apoſtolike Romane See, pro- ſtoral care & miſed that after his departure he vvould not ceaſe to pray for him & his flocke, thereby to protection of eaſe him of his Paſtoral burden. To. I Concil. p. S. Clem. in initio. And S. Leo the Great the Church af one of his ſue ceſſors n theſaid See, often attrue the good admnaton and gouer- ter his death. nement thereof to Peters praiers and aſsiſtance: namnely in theſe goodly vvordes Ser. The Saincts in heauen pray for the liuing Feaſtes of ho in anniuerſ. die aſſumpt. ad Poutif. We are much bound (ſaith he) to giue thankes Lordand Redeemer Ieſus Chriſt, that hath giuen ſo great povver to him vuhom hemade the Prince of the vvhole Church: chat if in our time alſo auy thing be done vvel ho ri ghily ordered by vs, it is to be imputed to hi vvorkes and his gouernement, to vuhom it vuas ſaid, And thou being conuerted, confirme thy Gagn. Lue. brethren:and vuhom our Lord after hu reſurrection ſaid thriſe. I eede my ſheepe. Which nowt.21. alſo vuithout daube the godly Paſtor doth execute, confirming vs vvith his exhortations, and nat ceaſing to pray for vs, that vde be ouercome vuith no tentation. &c. Yea it vvas a common thing in the primitiue Church among the auncient Chriſtians, and alvvaies ſince among the faithful, to make couenant in their life time, that vvhether of them vvent to heauen before the other, he ſ hould pray for his frende and fellovv yet aliue. See the Eccle- ſiaſtical hiſtorie of the holy virgin and Martyr Potamiana, promiſing at the houre of her Mar- tyrdom, that after her death ſhe vvould procure mercie of God to Baſilides one of the ſouldiars that ledde her to execution, and ſo ſhe did. Euſch. li. 6.e. Alſo S. Cyprian. in fine. Let vs, (ſaith he) pray mutually one for an other, and vuhether of us tudo ſhal hy Gods clemencie be firſt called for, let his laue continue, and his praier not ceaſe for his brethren and ſiſters in the vvorld. So ſaid this holy Martyr at that time vvhen Chriſtiās vvere ſo far from Caluiniſme (vvhich abhorreth the praiers of Saincts & praying to them) that to be ſure, they bargained before hād to haue the martyrs & other Saincts to pray for them. The ſame S. Cyprian alſo in his booke De diſciplinavrginum, nfine, after a godly exhortation made to the holy Virgins or Nonnes in his time, ſpeaketh thus vnto them: Tantum tunc mementote noſtri, cum inipiet dobis dirginitas honorari. that is,, Onely then haue vs in rememhrance, vvhen your virginitis ( hal begin to be honoured. that is, after their departure. Vvhere he inſinuateth the vſe of the Catholike Church in keeping the feſtiual daies and other dueties tovvard the holy Wirgins in heauen. S. Hierom alſo in the ſame manner ſpeaketh to Helio- dorus, ſaying, that vvhen he is once in heauen, then he vvil pray for him that exhorted and incite d him to the bleſſed ſtate of the Monaſtical life. Ep. e. And ſo doth he ſpeake to the vertuous matrone Paula aſter her death, deſiring her to pray for Inuocation of him in his old age, affirining that ſhe ſhal the moie caſily obtaine, the neerer ſhe is novvioyned Chriſt in heaue. in Epitaph. Paule in fine. It vvere to long to report, hovv S. Auguſtine deſireth to be holpen by S. Cyprians praiers (then and long before a Sainct in heauen) to the vnderſtanding ofthe truth concerning the peace and regiment of the Church. li.dBapt.Doa.
